$comment: Every deliberate difference between git-ticket-canvas (desk) and git-ticket-canvas-server (served). Asserted by web/src/ui/canvas-parity.test.tsx and internal/api/parity_test.go: a difference not named here fails, and a name here that is no longer a difference fails too. Run both with `just drift-check`.

chrome.reason: It opens the session dialog, and a desk canvas has no session to describe or to end. App offers it on session.authenticated, which GET /api/session answers false for on a desk canvas because signOn builds no provider for it. A desk canvas showing an account button would be offering to log out of nothing.

It reports that writes are refused, and follows the board's readOnly rather than the command. This is a difference in default, not in capability: -read-only defaults true on served and false on desk, and either canvas shows the badge when it is set. Declared at the shape the commands actually ship in, because that is the pair a person compares.

routes.reason: Which actor a person writes under. A desk canvas resolves one when a store opens, so there is nobody to ask and nothing to choose; registering a route it would always refuse would be adding surface for nothing.
Binds a signed-in subject to an actor id. Meaningless without a subject, and a desk canvas has none.
The unprefixed form of the same thing, for a canvas serving exactly one store.
The unprefixed form of the same thing, for a canvas serving exactly one store.
Every account that has signed in, read by administrators. A desk canvas records no logins, so it has nothing to answer and no administrator to answer to.

notLookedAt: A control with no id. Giving one is how this codebase marks something addressable, so the chrome test treats an id as the definition of an identified control; a difference in unidentified markup is not caught.

The store picker, which is not a difference between the commands. It appears whenever GET /api/stores returns anything, so a desk canvas over several repositories shows it too. The chrome test holds the store count equal across both shapes so that this does not get reported as a difference between the commands when it is a difference in how many stores are configured.
Refusals. A route that exists and answers 401 or 403 is reachable for this purpose; who may use it is an access question, covered by internal/api/access_test.go.
